unit.title: Deterministic Round-Robin Scheduler Simulator in C
unit.scope: A self-contained prerequisite bridge from algorithmic reasoning to defensive C, deterministic state transitions, testing, and technical documentation. It is not represented as a UC Berkeley CS162 lecture, homework, or project.
unit.audience: A strong algorithms student with working C, command-line, Make, and basic debugger skills
learning_objectives: Turn scheduling rules into explicit state, invariants, and deterministic tie-breaking behavior.
Separate scheduling policy from queue, parsing, reporting, and error-handling mechanisms.
Implement a bounded C command-line program with checked parsing, ownership discipline, and overflow-aware arithmetic.
Create repeatable tests that exercise normal traces, ties, idle time, malformed input, and boundary values.
Record design decisions and reproducible validation evidence.

required_evidence: The submitted program builds through the documented non-interactive command.
Automated tests and recorded commands are reproducible in the evaluator's environment.
The implementation satisfies the public behavioral contract and rejects invalid input.
The design note, test inventory, and comprehension responses are present.
completion_policy.decision_rule: Only independent validation of the required evidence may mark unit_kickoff_rrsim_v1 complete. Passing this unit changes no claim about later CS162 units, the full catalog course, or institutional credit.
